facts.claim: Under FAA Part 103, a qualifying ultralight vehicle can be flown in the United States without a pilot certificate, aircraft registration, airworthiness certification, or medical certification.

For powered ultralights, the FAA limits empty weight to 254 lb (115.2 kg), fuel capacity to five gallons (18.9 liters), maximum level-flight speed to 55 knots, and maximum power-off stall speed to 24 knots; they are limited to a single occupant and to sport or recreational purposes.
Unpowered ultralights, such as many hang gliders, must weigh less than 155 pounds (70.3 kg) empty under Part 103.

Ultralight operations are generally limited to daylight hours, must avoid congested areas, cities, towns and open-air assemblies, and are restricted within controlled airspace (Class A, B, C, D, E and most special use airspace) unless prior authorization has been obtained from air traffic control.

Ultralight aircraft are not governed by either 14 CFR Part 61 or Part 91, and Advisory Circular AC-91-36D suggests ultralight pilots voluntarily remain above 2,000 feet above ground level wherever possible.

The Experimental Aircraft Association promotes structured training programs for ultralight pilots, and Pilot Institute has highlighted that knowledge of weather, aerodynamics and operating limitations remains critical for safe flight.

Flight training for a Private Pilot License can range from $9,000 to $130,000, while Aerocorner reports the cheapest new ultralight aircraft in 2026 is the Mini-Max 1103R kit, listed at $10,899.99 for the airframe with a finished ready-to-fly example at about $22,500.

zh.title: 美國Part 103超輕型飛機免駕照 限重254磅、僅限單座日間飛行
zh.summary: 美國聯邦航空總署Part 103規定，符合條件的超輕型飛行器無須駕照、註冊、適航證或體檢即可飛行，但空重須低於254磅、限單座、日間目視飛行，且不得飛越人群與管制空域。
body: 在美國，駕駛飛機通常需要駕照、體檢與飛機註冊，但聯邦航空總署Part 103為超輕型飛行器留了一個狹窄例外：符合條件的飛行器無須駕駛執照、飛機註冊、適航認證或體檢即可飛行。這項豁免是為了支持休閒飛行，同時以嚴格的飛機性能限制來控制風險。
動力超輕型飛行器的上限十分明確：空重低於254磅（115.2公斤）、油量上限5加侖（18.9公升）、平飛極速55節、無動力失速速度上限24節，且僅限單人乘坐、僅供運動與休閒用途。無動力超輕型飛行器（如懸掛式滑翔機）空重則須低於155磅（70.3公斤）。這些限制使超輕型飛行器無法演變為一般需要認證與駕駛資格的飛機。
免照不等於無法管。Part 103飛行器仍受聯邦航空法規的運作限制：僅限日間飛行、須保持對地面的目視參考並符合目視飛航天氣標準，不得飛越擁擠地區、城鎮或露天人群集會；除非事先取得航管許可，不得進入管制空域（A、B、C、D、E類及多數特殊用途空域）。實驗航空協會（EAA）等團體仍建議接受正規訓練，諮詢通告AC-91-36D亦建議超輕型飛行員盡可能保持在地面2000英尺以上。
門檻低是Part 103歷久不衰的原因：私人飛行執照訓練費用約9000至130000美元，超輕型飛行器的購置與訓練成本則低得多。據Aerocorner統計，2026年最便宜的新款超輕型飛行器是Mini-Max 1103R木布結構套件，機身售價10899.99美元，整機即飛版約22500美元。但低門檻伴隨妥協：航程短、速度慢、對天氣敏感，且單座設計使飛行員無法搭載乘客或教練同行。

en.title: Why a Part 103 ultralight aircraft needs no pilot's license in the US
en.summary: Under FAA Part 103, a qualifying ultralight vehicle can be flown in the United States without a pilot certificate, registration, airworthiness approval or medical — but only within strict weight, speed, fuel and operating limits.
body: Many people assume that flying any aircraft requires extensive training, a pilot certificate, medical approval and federal registration. The Federal Aviation Administration has long maintained a narrow exception: under Part 103, certain recreational flyers can take to the skies without a pilot license. The exception applies only to a highly specific category of lightweight recreational aircraft that must meet strict performance, weight and operating requirements.

For powered ultralights, the FAA limits empty weight to 254 lb (115.2 kg), fuel capacity to five gallons (18.9 liters), maximum level-flight speed to 55 knots, and maximum power-off stall speed to 24 knots. Qualifying vehicles are intended solely for sport and recreational purposes and are limited to a single occupant. Unpowered ultralights, such as many hang gliders, must weigh less than 155 pounds (70.3 kg) empty. Because these aircraft are intentionally small and limited in capability, the FAA regulates them differently than conventional airplanes.

Operators are exempt from licensing requirements, but they are not exempt from federal aviation regulations. Operations are generally limited to daylight hours and must avoid congested areas, cities, towns and open-air assemblies of people, and ultralights are restricted from controlled airspace — Class A, B, C, D, E and most special use airspace — unless prior authorization has been obtained from air traffic control. Notably, ultralight aircraft are not governed by either 14 CFR Part 61 or Part 91. Aviation groups such as the Experimental Aircraft Association encourage structured training, and Advisory Circular AC-91-36D suggests ultralight pilots voluntarily remain above 2,000 feet above ground level wherever possible.

Cost is another reason Part 103 endures. Flight training for a Private Pilot License can range from $9,000 to $130,000, while ultralight flying has a far lower barrier to entry. Aerocorner reports that the cheapest new ultralight aircraft in 2026 is the Mini-Max 1103R, a single-seat wood-and-fabric kit that Mini-Max USA lists at $10,899.99 for the airframe, with a finished, ready-to-fly example at about $22,500. The trade-off is capability: limited range, lower speed, weather sensitivity, and a single-seat design that prevents carrying passengers or instructors during normal operations.
